# M0-S5 I1: the cgo policy follows the target module, not the starting
# directory. `logos -C <dir>` honors the cgo policy of the module at <dir>,
# and in a workspace each main module's own logos.toml governs its packages.
# The script starts in a forbid loGo/s module; every case below must still
# apply the target's policy.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# Default CC: a host compiler setting must not drive the build.
env CC=

# Case 1: the allow loGo/s module at b/ builds its cgo program via -C,
# even though the starting directory is a forbid module.
env CGO_ENABLED=
[cgo] logos -C b run .
[cgo] stdout '^b: 42$'

# Case 2: a plain Go cgo module via -C builds with the upstream default
# (CGO_ENABLED stays unset). The cgo key of the starting module has no
# effect on it.
env CGO_ENABLED=
[cgo] logos -C g run .
[cgo] stdout '^g: 42$'

# Case 3: workspace w/ with an allow loGo/s module (ma) and a no-key loGo/s
# module (mb). ma's cgo package builds; mb's fails with the forbid text.
env CGO_ENABLED=
[cgo] logos -C w run example.com/ma
[cgo] stdout '^ma: 42$'
[cgo] ! logos -C w run example.com/mb
[cgo] stderr '\[restriction::cgo_usage\] cgo is disabled'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/a

go 1.27

-- logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "forbid"

-- main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("a") }

-- b/go.mod --
module example.com/b

go 1.27

-- b/logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "allow"

-- b/main.lgo --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("b:", C.answer()) }

-- g/go.mod --
module example.com/g

go 1.27

-- g/main.go --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("g:", C.answer()) }

-- ma/go.mod --
module example.com/ma

go 1.27

-- ma/logos.toml --
[build]
cgo = "allow"

-- ma/main.lgo --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("ma:", C.answer()) }

-- mb/go.mod --
module example.com/mb

go 1.27

-- mb/main.lgo --
package main

/*
int answer() { return 42; }
*/
import "C"

import "fmt"

func main() { fmt.Println("mb:", C.answer()) }

-- w/go.work --
go 1.27

use (
	../ma
	../mb
)
